import * as C from "@constants";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";

{C.TIMESCALE_DB} uses approximation algorithms to calculate a percentile without
requiring all of the data. This also makes them more compatible with {C.CAGG}s.

By default, {C.TOOLKIT_LONG} uses `uddsketch`, but you can also choose to use
`tdigest`. For more information about these algorithms, see the
[advanced aggregation methods](/build/data-management/hyperfunctions/percentile-approx/advanced-agg) documentation.

## Run an approximate percentage query

In this procedure, we use an example table called `response_times` that contains
information about how long a server takes to respond to API calls.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Create a ${C.CAGG} for daily aggregates`}>
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW response_times_daily
WITH (timescaledb.continuous)
AS SELECT
  time_bucket('1 day'::interval, ts) as bucket,
  percentile_agg(response_time_ms)
FROM response_times
GROUP BY 1;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Query the ninety-fifth percentile over the last 30 days">
Re-aggregate the aggregate to get the last 30 days:

```sql
SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, percentile_agg) as threshold
FROM response_times_daily
WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval);
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create an alert">
```sql
WITH t as (SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, percentile_agg(percentile_agg)) as threshold
FROM response_times_daily
WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval))

SELECT count(*)
FROM response_times
WHERE ts > now()- '1 minute'::interval
AND response_time_ms > (SELECT threshold FROM t);
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

For more information about percentile approximation API calls, see the
[hyperfunction API documentation](/reference/toolkit/percentile-approximation/uddsketch/percentile_agg).
